t: Warsaw grew from a fishing village into the seat of the Dukes of Masovia, and became the capital of the Polish Crown and the Commonwealth when Sigismund III moved his court from Kraków in 1596.
After the partitions it was held by Prussia, ruled as the Duchy of Warsaw and Congress Poland, and then by Russia, until it became the capital of independent Poland on 11 November 1918.
In the Second World War its Jewish population was confined in a ghetto and two uprisings were crushed, and about 85% of the city was destroyed; the Old Town was rebuilt after the war.
dyk: In 1647 Valerianus Magnus performed a vacuum experiment in Warsaw, repeating Torricelli's, which contradicted official European science.

f.founded: The Prince of Płock, Bolesław II of Masovia, established the city in about 1300 on the site of a small fishing village called Warszowa; the first document attesting a castellany there dates to 1313.
f.where: On both banks of the Vistula in the Masovian Plain in east-central Poland, about 260 km from the Baltic Sea and 523 km east of Berlin.
f.known: Seat of the Dukes of Masovia; capital of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth from 1596; the Warsaw Confederation of 1573; the Constitution of 3 May 1791; the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising of 1943 and the Warsaw Uprising of 1944; the rebuilt Old Town
f.today: Warsaw is the capital and most populous city of Poland and the capital of the Masovian Voivodeship, with about 1.87 million residents.
